text:
kevin: quick RFC follow-up — after reading the feedback on the service-binding proposal, I want to clarify our current plan and surface a couple tradeoffs. do we want project-scoped api keys to remain the default for user-created keys, with org-scoped keys only for infra/ops?
sasha: +1 to defaults, but we should be clear about cross-project service workers. many infra flows need org-wide access (eg metrics ingestion).
maria: are we still leaning on two primitives: long-lived \"attach\" keys (bounded by project/org) and short-lived brokered tokens for runtime actions?
dan: that was the intent in the RFC. long-lived keys are mainly for human/CI onboarding; runtime services should use ephemeral tokens minted by a broker with narrower claims.
kevin: right. main tradeoffs:
- long-lived keys are simple but increase blast radius if leaked.
- ephemeral tokens reduce blast radius but add broker complexity and latency.
maria: latency shouldn't be a deal-breaker if the broker is colocated and caches auth decisions. we already have that pattern in a few places.
sasha: question: how do we express RBAC for org-scoped keys? current model is project:<project_id>:role. org role would be org:<org_id>:role. need to be explicit about precedence when both claims exist.
dan: prefer explicit precedence: token-specific (project) > org-wide > default. so if token has project claim, it trumps org RBAC. simplifies checks.
kevin: agreed, project claims should override. but we also want a policy for service-role binding where a service principal can be bound to multiple projects/orgs. sample claim: { aud: \"inference\", iss: \"auth-broker\", sub: \"svc-prod-ingest\", claims: [\"project:123:writer\",\"org:555:metrics_writer\"] }
sasha: make sure role resolution is idempotent for rollout. if a service is bound to project A and org B, we evaluate both but deny unless at least one grants the verb.
maria: also need a migration path for existing api keys. suggestion: shadow-check mode for 30 days where we accept both legacy keys and new-scoped keys but log divergences.
kevin: yes — migration plan idea:
1) implement broker + policy evaluator behind feature flag (dev only)
2) rollout org-scoped key creation UI + CLI opt-in
3) enable shadow-check for existing API keys and produce weekly divergence reports (security + infra)
4) after 30–60 days, require explicit scoping for new keys; old keys get expiration/rotation prompts
5) final cutover: rotate legacy keys with an automated agent or org-admin approval
dan: sounds good. one more piece: how to treat service-to-service call patterns where caller has only org claim but needs project-limited side effects? e.g., infra agent writing user metrics for project X but only has org scope.
sasha: we can support one-off project impersonation via the broker: caller requests a short-lived claim scoped to project X if it proves the necessary predicate (audit token, owner approval, or signed grant).
maria: we should limit impersonation to well-audited routes and log every grant. also surface TTLs: default ephemeral token TTL = 1h, max 24h for special approvals.
kevin: noted. operational concerns: quota and cost. broker minting per-request could increase billing for high-throughput services. caching of grants and issuance of reusable ephemeral sessions helps.
dan: recommend we add caching layer keyed by (caller, requested_scope, resource) with short TTL (30s–2m) and ability to revoke by listing active grants in console.
sasha: inline example for RBAC check pseudocode:
```
# token.claims: [\"project:123:writer\"]
if has_claim(token, \"project:${id}:${role}\"):
  allow
elif has_claim(token, \"org:${org_id}:${role}\"):
  allow
else:
  deny
```
maria: small security nit: forbid embedding admin roles into long-lived keys. admin-level privileges must go through SSO flows and be ephemeral. long-lived keys can be \"owner-lite\" with limited perms.
kevin: agreed. action items:
- dan: prototype broker + policy evaluator, include caching and revoke list (ETA 2w)
- sasha: update RBAC model doc with explicit precedence and impersonation rules (ETA 1w)
- maria: draft migration/shadow-check runbook + reporting dashboard fields (ETA 1w)
- kevin: coordinate with console & CLI team for UI/UX feature flag path (ETA 2w)
auth-bot: created ticket INF-4321 for \"service-binding broker prototype\" assigned to dan, priority P2
kevin: thanks. can we also schedule a short sync next Tue to unblock any API surface questions? 30m should do it.
sasha: yes — I'll send an invite. :calendar: 
maria: leaving a note — think about telemetry: include token source (long-lived vs brokered) in request logs for cost attribution.
dan: will add. one question outstanding: default behavior for org-admins creating keys via API — should the API require an explicit parameter \"scope=org\"?
sasha: require it. fail-open is dangerous. API should reject ambiguous requests with 400 + explanation.
kevin: ok, cool. moving this to RFC follow-up doc after sync. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
